This is a terrible article.

How it works is that space and time are put on equal footing in a four-dimensional space-time. The location of every event has a set of four-dimensional coordinates. Consider an event that releases a flash of light, followed by another event that absorbs it. Measure the space distance between the two events, then measure the time interval between them. Divide the space distance by the time interval. This has been done and we find that everyone gets the same number, the speed of light, even for observers that are moving in any direction and speed.

There is no known reason for this. It just appears to be the way the universe works. You can create theoretical universes without this rule and they are perfectly sensible, they are just not our universe.

The math behind it is simple high school algebra. If you can handle that, then you can puzzle your way through a book on special relativity.

One of the consequences is that if everybody measures the same speed of light in every experiment, then something has to give. What gives turns out to be clocks. Identical clocks will appear to run at different speeds if they are in relative motion.
